questions.q: How does this lesson's question build on Scripting & Application Development's scoped application basics?
options: That course covered how one scoped application isolates itself; this lesson asks how many an instance should have and where their boundaries should fall
This lesson replaces the need for sys_scope entirely
Scoped applications are no longer isolated once an instance reaches enterprise scale
The two topics are unrelated
questions.explain: The mechanics of isolation were already covered; this lesson is about the enterprise-scale question of how many scopes to maintain and where to draw their edges.

questions.q: What is a real cost of having too many narrowly-scoped applications on one instance?
options: There is no real cost — more scopes is always strictly better
More separate upgrade-testing efforts and more cross-app integration points to manage, often for splits that don't reflect any real organizational boundary
Narrow scopes make Domain Separation unnecessary
Narrow scopes eliminate the need for Cross-Scope Access Controls entirely
questions.explain: Dozens of tiny scopes multiply regression-testing effort and cross-scope dependency management, sometimes for a split made too early.

questions.q: What is the real risk of bundling unrelated functionality into one giant, overly broad scoped application?
options: Genuine coupling and blast-radius risk — a bug introduced fixing one feature can break every other feature bundled into the same scope, since they deploy and roll back together
No risk at all, since Global scope absorbs any blast radius
It only affects performance, never reliability
It makes Application Repository versioning unnecessary
questions.explain: Features bundled into one scope all deploy, upgrade, and roll back as a single unit, so a bug anywhere in it can affect everything else bundled in.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what should actually decide where a scope boundary falls?
options: Alphabetical convenience in naming
A genuine functional and ownership boundary — the edge where one team builds, tests, and deploys independently of another
Whichever boundary minimizes the number of tables in a scope
Scope boundaries should be decided by table count alone
questions.explain: The practical guidance ties scope boundaries to real team ownership and independent release cadence, not arbitrary convenience.

questions.q: Why does dependency pinning via Application Repository versioning matter once an org has several interdependent scoped apps?
options: It is purely optional busywork with no real effect
Pinning a dependency to a specific published version prevents a breaking change in one scoped app from silently breaking another that depends on it
It replaces the need for scope boundaries entirely
It only matters for a single, standalone scoped application
questions.explain: Consuming a pinned version instead of always-latest is what lets independent teams move fast in their own scope without breaking everyone else's.
